village: Space, Foundational Advance, Software & AI, Biomanufacturing
tagline: A stress-responsive optogenetic bioreactor that predicts crop stress from field sensors and forecasts, then uses green light to make plant-protective proteins on the farm.
summary: ReLEAF closes a loop: field sensors and weather forecasts feed a stress-index model, the model sets a green-light dose, green light drives the cyanobacterial CcaSR two-component system in Bacillus subtilis WB800, and the cells secrete ACC deaminase into a hollow-fiber perfusion bioreactor that lets protein out and keeps cells in. The unit is about 40 x 24 x 62 cm, designed to stand beside a Taiwanese smallholder paddy where the average agricultural manager is 63.8 years old and precision agriculture is otherwise out of reach. It swept the high-school technical awards (Measurement, Hardware, Integrated Human Practices) largely on provenance discipline: four self-built devices with release build manuals, a digital twin that caught a failing photometer 26.7 hours before it died, a pre-registered growth forecast scored against a later run, and an input ledger that marks every number as measured, cited or modelled. Its distinguishing quality is honesty — the wiki repeatedly withdraws its own claims, and that is also where its dry-lab weaknesses are visible.
awards: Best Integrated Human Practices winner (High School)
Best Village Project nominee (Space / Foundational Advance / Software & AI / Biomanufacturing)

dry.frameworks: Four strands. (1) A fitted crop-stress index: rather than weighting temperature, water and light by expert judgement, they fitted weights to Taiwan's own harvest record — 25 years of county rice yields from the Agriculture and Food Agency against ERA5 daily reanalysis weather (2001-2025), treating a season below the county trend as a stressed season, and exhaustively scoring all 2^15 - 1 = 32,767 combinations of fifteen candidate stress terms on held-out years. First and second rice crops were fitted separately; the second crop pays for wind, light and badly timed water, and heat adds nothing once those three are in — which the wiki notes undercuts the wet lab's heat programme. County error over 2016-2025 was 365 kg/ha against 419 for a plain trend line (32% error reduction on the second crop). A genuinely prospective test was frozen on 26 September 2026 before any county published; four of sixteen counties reported at 7.9% error against the trend's 8.8%, which the team correctly calls too few to establish performance. (2) Protein design (the GRAFT methodology: Generate, Restraints, Assembly, Flex, Triage) selected and shaped three protectants before any cloning — BoPEP4 (a 23-aa Brassica oleracea plant elicitor peptide docked against the PEPR1 receptor and run as nine all-atom MD trajectories), LEA14 (151-aa late embryogenesis abundant protein, five N-His constructs including a borrowed K-segment membrane-binding motif joined by a GGGGS linker), and ACC deaminase. The standout findings are negative and caught in time: a C-terminal 6xHis purification tag that every earlier check had approved was shown in simulation to cap the chemical group forming the peptide's strongest receptor contact, so the tag moved to the N-terminus; an Asn23 clamp was found to be five contacts rather than one salt bridge; a truncation ladder identified 9-23 as the production length (33% less mass) with the grip holding 98.5% of frames for 7-23 against 77.1% for the next rung down; and an AlphaFold confidence gate set before the result came back was failed for LEA14 with its partner, so by prior agreement no structure was handed on. For ACC deaminase no mutant was ordered at all, because the modelling said the enzyme meets far less substrate than it could handle and the largest available gain is a change to the medium (apoplast pH 5.5, where the Glu12-His227 contact holds in 99.9% of frames). (3) A reactor digital twin: an autoencoder trained on the healthy first 120 hours of a 434-hour run, scoring a sensor axis (the reference beam, which never passes through the culture) separately from a process axis (specific growth rate), so it can distinguish a culture event from a failing instrument; plus a Kalman-filter batch forecaster and a logistic growth prior fitted from the light plate. (4) Dose and fleet models: an arithmetic ledger from millilitres on a petri dish to US dollars per hectare, and a payback curve plotted across the whole efficacy axis.
dry.dataviz: The wiki's signature device is provenance colour-coding. The M4 dose ledger is drawn as a single top-to-bottom chain from 1.67 mL on a 10 cm plate to US$3800 capital per hectare, with a rail down the left that is green while every row still rests on a measurement and turns amber at the rice canopy correction, so a reader can see exactly where measurement stops and modelling begins; rows below inherit the model and two add assumptions of their own. Every model input is tabulated with a provenance column (seven from their own bench, four public records, two published constants, one from Geospatial Analysis, one neither measured nor cited), and the five assumptions get a table of 'what rests on it' and 'what would overturn it'. A timing diagram overlays the three-day Central Weather Administration forecast horizon, the three arrival arms the plant team ran, and the 5.4-day reactor lead time on a days-from-stress axis to show visually that they do not fit. The three disagreeing timing runs are shown side by side with the third panel re-reading the middle panel's own tubes as total chlorophyll instead of per gram, so the ranking visibly reverses — the figure argues against the team's own earlier claim. Decay figures plot both candidate interpretations through the same 28-hour reading and label the 22-fold divergence ('What one endpoint cannot say'). The payback plot marks their own 68-years-at-efficacy-1 point and Geospatial Analysis's 4.9-year estimate on the same axis and names the disagreement rather than hiding it. The digital twin UI itself puts optical density, pH, four pressure traces and the pump and valve controls on one screen; the description page opens with an interactive seven-block system map and a GIS choropleth of county nighttime temperature with circles scaled by rice yield trend.
dry.datascience: Three practices lift this above typical high-school dry lab. First, pre-registration: on 1 October, before any WB800 bioreactor run, they registered a specific growth rate of 0.2986 h^-1 with a 90% interval of 0.2705-0.3300, a logistic curve shape with an NRMSE pass threshold of 15%, and inoculum-conditional times to OD 0.5, together with stated pass criteria. Run 6 gave 0.286 +/- 0.010 h^-1 (R2 0.978), inside the interval; the curve-shape endpoint was recorded as not scored because the prior misses the first seven hours by 30% and the run passes the prior's ceiling before hour 7. Run 7 was explicitly excluded from scoring because its three-hour lag has no term in the registered logistic and its fitted rate swings 0.16-0.46 h^-1 with the window choice. Second, anomaly detection with a diagnostic split: the autoencoder flagged the photometer at 216.3 h, 26.7 h before the OD channel failed at 243.0 h, and the window table shows the sensor axis at 100% alarms with the process axis at 0% during the drift — the model names which subsystem is broken, not just that something is. Third, forecast benchmarking against persistence rather than against nothing: the Kalman filter beat a no-change baseline by 41% at 2 h on the September run and by 24% at 8 and 12 h on run 7, with global-linear, exponential and local-linear alternatives reported as losers and the honest caveat that most of the run is above the photometer's linear range so the model forecasts the reading, not biomass. Other measurement work: the in-line photometer tracks a benchtop BioDrop with slope 1.018 (R2 0.995) to OD 1.2 across 45 paired TiO2 points and an iGEM silica protocol run in 2.5 mg steps, with a dilute-and-restore test returning within 0.2%; wall shear computed from pressure sensors and from the flow meter agree to 2.8%, so each sensor checks the other; and leaf-sensor bench characterisation found a +0.47 to +1.71 degC site-dependent offset against the air reference across 540 paired readings, with the conclusion stated that a 1.2-1.9 degC bias can hide or invent the very water-stress signal the twin would act on. Honest dry-lab weaknesses, stated by the team: a secreted-activity figure of 7.25 mU/mL at n = 1 and below quantitation; two induction runs that disagree on the sign of activity change over hours; the published CcaSR Hill curve (Castillo-Hair et al. 2019) assumed valid at 20 L when every induction was run at a single light intensity, so nothing tests it; a rice canopy correction of x2.44 that is modelled, not measured, and spans 1.68-3.52; a minimum effective dose that is unknown because the spray experiment varied salt and timing but never the applied amount; a withdrawn efficacy coefficient of 0.58; and only 17 of 25 modelled seasons ever crossing the trigger, so a ten-unit fleet runs on 4.3% of the calendar.
dry.software: The digital twin is released MIT-licensed at https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/gems-taiwan/digital-twin. It reads live OD600, pH, four pressure channels and turbine flow from the reactor loop, drives a pinch valve and four Luer valves, runs the autoencoder sensor alarm and the Kalman batch forecast, computes lumen pressure drop, transmembrane pressure and a fouling ratio through a hydraulic model, and applies the BLASTAM leaf-blast infection rule (a wet period counts when the leaf stays wet at least 10 hours at a mean of 22-25 degC, no infection below 15 or above 25 degC, past hours from the sensor and future hours estimated as wet at 90% relative humidity) to tell a grower to look for lesions five to ten days later. The team is clear about what is not wired up: green-light induction is tested but not integrated, dissolved-oxygen calibration did not hold, the protectant amount cannot be read in-line and comes from hand-drawn ELISA and DNPH samples, and every model so far has run on recorded data after a run with a person making every decision — so it is honestly a digital shadow moving toward a twin. Four open hardware devices ship with build manuals and print files: the hollow-fiber perfusion bioreactor (10-page assembly guide, 17-page brochure, 16-page user manual), a Pro and a Slim in-line photometer (12- and 13-page guides), and a 24-tube dual-wavelength light plate apparatus (10-page guide), plus a floating hydroponics plate with 13 seed positions, a 6.5 MB hardware notebook covering 23 March to 17 October 2026, and an LLM-assisted QGIS geospatial workflow over 346 farming townships with the data-preparation prompt published. Also contributed: 35 Registry parts in five SubtiToolKit Golden Gate modules, a 15-page plant protocol, a twentyfold scale-down of the ACC deaminase DNPH activity assay onto a 96-well plate, and waste-media protocols (hay, okara and sugarcane extracts benchmarked against LB).

good.publicEngagement: 140 students across 5 schools in tiered lessons for elementary, junior high and high school audiences, with pre- and post-Kahoot surveys per cohort and the results published as per-question accuracy charts — including the failures, such as DNA base pairing where only 30% of students answered correctly. Everything is released on a dedicated education website: three lesson plans, three slide decks, two card games, two online games and a plant stress simulator (CropShield), free to download, with the stated aim of making the lessons work without the team in the room. Hands-on activities included plant stress experiments, planter making, an ATCG card game and vocabulary work. The team also edited its own claims down for honesty — a visible wiki comment records removing a '49-point' improvement claim and a 'standard teaching methods' comparison, and correcting a student count from 144 to 140. Separately, a Taiwan-specific engagement channel: a LINE official account called 'Nong You Zhu Shou' (Farmer's Assistant) with six functions — latest news, product introduction, crop stress alerts, a crop assistant AI chatbot keyed to terms like salinity, heat stress and pests, a Farmer's Diary where users post weather, crop photos, soil moisture and pest conditions and earn tokens redeemable for LINE stickers, and a Google Form feedback loop — built because interviews at the Farmer Expo and with Ms. Chen Hui-Wen showed smallholders could not reach the information that already exists online. A public event at Taipei Water Garden Organic Farmers' Market on 5 September 2026 (Taiwan Coffee x Cocoa Gelato Festival) drew over 400 visitors with over 200 registered participants, running a forum, booth activities including a data-physicalisation installation and a ring toss, and a plant stress event.
good.ihp: 31 stakeholders over seven months, structured as a project evolution map in four stages with named dates, plus four thematic expert pipelines (deployment, protectant design, plant and stress biology, bioreactor and hardware) and continuous engagement with five core experts. The decisive change came at the very start: the original design released engineered Bacillus subtilis into the soil with a DesK-DesR system reading temperature directly. Prof. Chen Wen-Liang (10 April) and bioprocess experts said two things were wrong — the bacteria could not be contained, and biological sensing was neither precise nor controllable enough — so sensing moved out of the cell into electronic sensors and an AIoT model, and a hollow-fiber perfusion bioreactor was built to hold the bacteria in while letting the protectants out. That one conversation produced the entire architecture. Other changes with a clear before/after: Dr. Paul Verslues (Academia Sinica, 3 April) argued that supplying pure proline is inefficient and risks suppressing the plant's own P5CS1 biosynthesis and proline-redox balance, so they abandoned proline delivery for a plant-regulation framework using bacterial signals and precursors, shifted from stress recovery to early detection, and re-scored outcomes on root growth and biomass. Dr. Elizabeth Sattely (Stanford, 27 June) told them their proof of concept was too broad and to do one stress very well instead of many superficially, and to look at peptides — which is why BoPEP4 entered the panel and why plant testing narrowed to heat and salinity. CH Biotech (9 July) pushed them toward computational screening to optimise protectants, comparison of root irrigation vs foliar vs drone spray, production cost per area, and Taiwanese regulatory research before acting. Prof. Huang Chieh-Chen (NCHU, 28 July and 6 August) moved the reactor from continuous to periodic operation, raised seedling-stage application, warned that excessive protectant concentrations harm plants so thresholds must be validated, and supplied the B. subtilis WB800 strain the project now runs on. Prof. Cheng Mei-Chun (28 August) found that inconsistent plant ages and treatment conditions meant earlier results may have reflected unintended stress rather than treatment, and the protocols were standardised in response. Yes Health iFarm (11 August) prompted reconsidering the 8/16 light cycle for 12/12, adding DO and OD to parameter planning, switching from pure oxygen to gentle aeration, and minimising transplants because transplantation itself is a stressor. Most interesting is the natural-farming thread: at a public forum co-hosted with Green Media on 5 September, Dr. Li Hsu-Ying and Ms. Chen argued that a plant protected from every stress never builds tolerance — 'raising a crop is like raising a child'. Rather than dismiss it, the team made that the specification for M1: the reactor should fire only when a threshold that genuinely reflects crop condition is crossed, which is why the 32% error reduction matters as evidence for a release rule rather than as a number. A farmer at the same forum asked whether the system breaks organic certification; the team researched the regulations and concluded it cannot be used on organic farms, then interviewed Mr. Chen Ke-Wei of the Lanyang River Friendly Farming Production Cooperative to work out what that means commercially. The project's origin question came from Ghanaian farmers via Gilbert Nkpeniyeng of Ubuntu Social Enterprise Ghana (1 February).
good.realWorld: Positioned as a social enterprise with the vision 'every farmer is a biomanufacturer', deployed through farmer collectives and pilot cooperatives rather than direct sales, because the fleet analysis shows a reactor owned by a single farm is idle most of the season. The MVP is costed component by component: current bioreactor US$2280, leaf humidity sensor US$125, a drop-in sealed bacteria cartridge US$90 that opens automatically once seated so no one handles an open culture, and a Field Console mobile app; capital works out at about US$3800 per hectare before refills, service or labour. The regulatory target is contained-use answers in Taiwan by October 2027, and the team worked the pathway with Director Wu Tzu-Hsien (12 October), who pointed out their cost model was missing factory, labour, bacterial cultivation and waste-management costs, and with Prof. Chang Hung-Hao (31 August), who told them to narrow the initial application to a specific stress and crop. A conversation with Bioeconomy Corporation at BIO Asia-Taiwan redirected expansion research toward Southeast Asia, where agricultural sectors are large and GMO rules looser than the US or EU. Smart Agriweek Taiwan identified young farmers as the realistic early adopters and flagged that older farmers need a separate persuasion route. SWOT and PESTLE analyses name the real threats plainly: unclear regulation for cell-free agricultural biologics that may fall between biological pesticide and synthetic-biology-derived compound; protectant washing away; biofouling reducing yield; and the fact that only 3.47% of Taiwan's farmland was organic or eco-friendly by 2024, which both bounds and shapes the market. The payback analysis is the most commercially honest thing on the wiki: on their own loss figure of US$138 per hectare per crop, no point on the efficacy axis returns the capital on a useful horizon — 68 years even at perfect efficacy — while Geospatial Analysis reaches 4.9 years from a net benefit of US$1931 per crop, and the team states that the two do not yet price the same hectare rather than quietly adopting the favourable number. Deliverables include an 85-page business plan, a farmer-friendly user manual, and the three bioreactor documents.

gemsTakeaway: The transferable asset is the provenance discipline, and it is cheaper than it looks: tag every number in a model as measured-by-us, cited, or modelled; publish an assumption register that states what would overturn each step; and when two of your own runs disagree, show both and name the disagreement instead of picking the flattering one. Pair that with one pre-registered, date-stamped prediction scored against a later experiment — GEMS-Taiwan's registered growth rate is the single highest-credibility item on its wiki, and it cost nothing but committing in writing before the data arrived.
